correctness.rationale: The proof gives exact definitions and quantifiers, derives the convolution concentration from a finite pair count, derives the variance formula directly, proves global strict monotonicity of variance, and treats the same-cell and different-cell cases exhaustively. The only published premise beyond the definition is that the central interval attains concentration for sums of the extremal family. The exact checker independently reconstructs the distributions on 8001 rational parameter pairs but is used only as a consistency check.

originality.rationale: The motivating paper states the unrestricted variance-equalization assertion as Conjecture 6.1 and identifies Kanter coverage only when every parameter is at least 1/2. The new theorem covers all positive parameters for exactly two summands, including the low-parameter cells, with an exact concentration formula and equality case. Claim-level published-finding corpus searches and primary-source comparisons found no stronger or equivalent indexed result. The residual risk is a poorly indexed elementary consequence of the same extremal family.
residual_risks: Because the proof is elementary once the extremal family is known, an equivalent two-summand argument may exist in poorly indexed notes or literature not surfaced by the searches.
No claim is made that database nonretrieval proves novelty; the assessment also rests on full-text inspection of the most directly relevant source.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the entire two-summand slice of an explicit published variance-equalization conjecture, including the parameter region below the known Kanter condition. The exact piecewise formula and strict equality classification expose the cell-boundary mechanism and are structurally relevant to higher-summand majorization attempts; this is not a routine isolated evaluation.
